latest_final: The puzzle turns on the double meaning of "courses." The student is at HKU, and the opening makes it sound as though his university class selections have vanished before the registration deadline. In fact, the university-course framing is misdirection. The "courses" that were gone were the food courses of a hall formal dinner he attended that evening. The meal was served as a succession of courses; he ate them, and the plates were cleared away as each course ended. By the end of the evening, all of those dinner courses had been consumed and removed—so "all of my courses were gone." Nothing happened to his university course selections, and the course-selection deadline was not genuinely involved; it merely set up the pun on "courses" as dishes rather than classes.
